Both traces tackle the logic puzzle by systematically testing possible positions for the "Rag" binding and the "1714/Leather" pair. Their approaches diverge significantly in accuracy and linearity. Trace 1 proceeds methodically, correctly eliminating impossible cases for Rag (e.g., slots 2, 4, 5) on the first pass and identifying slot 3 as the unique valid position. It then correctly eliminates invalid positions for 1714 (slots 1 and 5) and builds the solution without backtracking. Trace 2, conversely, initially mis-evaluates the cases. It erroneously eliminates the correct position for Rag (slot 3, labeled "Case 2") and later erroneously eliminates the correct position for 1714 (slot 2, labeled "Option 2b"). These false eliminations force Trace 2 to backtrack and re-evaluate these same cases, adding redundant work. For example, Trace 2 explicitly discards "Option 2b" due to a flawed deduction placing Ash in slot 3, only to later accept it when 1716 is correctly placed in slot 5. Trace 1 avoids these false starts and reaches the solution more efficiently.
